note: MutinyBIM standing performance gate. Budgets are set from measurements and only ever tightened; a budget is never raised to get green. Each row: p50 / p95 in its unit, its scope (in-process, browser, server) and cache state. How the gate reads them: scripts/perf/mutinybim/run.ts and docs/PERFORMANCE.md.

referenceHardware.reference: Current Apple-silicon developer laptop (M-series Pro/Max class, 16+ GB), plugged in, Chrome with hardware WebGL.
referenceHardware.weaker: Four-year-old integrated-GPU laptop. Approximated in the suite by 4x Chrome CPU throttling at 1366x768, devicePixelRatio 1; GPU is NOT throttled, so weak-laptop frame times are a lower bound until measured on real hardware.

regression.aggregation: Each run is a separate process. A run reports p50 and p95 of its own samples (one sample for cold metrics). The run-level figures are combined by taking the median across runs (median-of-N). Cold metrics: p50 = median of the runs, p95 = nearest-rank p95 of the runs.
regression.rule: A metric regresses when BOTH (current - baseline) > absFloor AND current > baseline * (1 + rel). Checked separately for p50 (rel.p50) and p95 (rel.p95). Baselines are compared only when the hardware class matches; otherwise the regression check reports NO-BASELINE and only absolute budgets apply.
regression.noisyRun: A run starting with 1-minute load average above 75% of the core count, or under 4 GB free memory, is marked noisy in the report. Noisy runs still count against absolute budgets; a regression seen only in a noisy run must be re-run before it blocks.

ci.why: A shared CI runner is not the reference laptop. On a calibrated runner (PERF_RUNNER) the gate enforces the structural invariants exactly and absolute timing budgets at budgetFactor x. On a shared runner (MUTINYBIM_PERF_BUDGETS=relative) it enforces invariants, sizes and same-run ratios, and reports timings without blocking. Regression bands apply only against a baseline recorded on the same hardware class.
